### Two things an agent needs and usually doesn't have

An agent that can only read what you paste into it is blind to everything else — it can't look something up, and it can't read a page you hand it a URL for. `awfind` and `awbrowse` are the two smallest possible answers to that: one client for search, one client for pages, both talking to a service you run rather than one you have to trust with your queries or your traffic.

### They are clients, not the service

Neither package ships a search engine or a browser. Each is a small, dependency-free wire client for a service *you* point it at — your own AitherSearch-shaped or AitherBrowser-shaped backend, self-hosted or otherwise. That split is deliberate: a client that quietly guessed an endpoint would be sending your queries and your pages somewhere you didn't choose, so both refuse outright without `--url`/`--token` (or the matching env var) set.

### Prove the contract before you prove the service

Both ship a `--self-test` that proves the wire contract with **no network at all** — the request shapes are right, the field names are right, nothing is silently dropped. That is the same trick every `aw*` client in this family uses: it separates "my install is broken" from "my service is unreachable", so a broken install fails loud immediately instead of on your first real query, days later, in front of someone you were demoing this to.

DO

1.  $ pip install awfind awbrowse
     you should see: Successfully installed awfind awbrowse
     if not: If `pip` is not found, install Python from python.org first (tick 'Add to PATH'), then open a NEW terminal and try again.
2.  $ awfind --self-test
     you should see: every check passes - offline, no service needed yet
     if not: This proves the CLIENT's own contract only; it needs no search service to pass. A failure here means the install itself is broken - try `pip install --force-reinstall awfind`.
3.  $ awbrowse --self-test
     you should see: same - the wire contract proven before you point it at anything
     if not: Same fix as above: `pip install --force-reinstall awbrowse`.
4. (optional)  $ awfind providers
     you should see: a list of configured search providers, from a real service
     if not: This one needs AWFIND_URL (or --url) pointing at an AitherSearch-shaped service you run. No service yet? Skip it - the self-test above already proved the client itself works, and this step will work the day you have one.

done when:  $ awfind --self-test
     you should see: no failures

WHAT YOU LEARNED

- Neither client guesses an endpoint. No --url/--token (or AWFIND_URL/AWBROWSE_URL, AWFIND_TOKEN/AWBROWSE_TOKEN) means it refuses rather than silently querying somewhere you did not choose.
- --self-test proves the wire contract with no network at all - the same trick every aw* client uses so a broken install fails LOUD instead of on your first real query.
- These are clients, not the service - point either at anything that speaks its wire contract, self-hosted or not.
